Hi Sasha — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Use case: structured extraction from support tickets + intent classification for routing.
- Current pain: latency spikes during peak, occasional classification drift after weekly model updates.
- Priority: precision on high-severity tickets (>95%) and predictable latency under 250ms P95.

What I promised on the call:
1) Recommended models & profiles: start with redwood/opt-7b-q4f and keep a pinned canary to redwood/opt-7b-q4f-v5.1 for high-priority routes; consider redwood/llama-3-13b for longer-context routing if latency allows.
2) Prompt set & benchmark links: attached prompt_set_v3.json and I uploaded the eval summary to our shared drive (link below).
3) Next steps: run a short backfill (1 week) on your prod sample, compare baseline metrics (precision/recall, hallucination rate) vs. post-update. If we see regressions, we can pin or rollback the serving variant while we investigate diffs.

Attachments: acme_eval_summary_q2.pdf, prompt_set_v3.json
Drive: https://redwood.app/drive/evals/acme-q2

Subject: Re: Fwd: regression report — quick validation + recommended mitigation

Quick triage notes after reproducing Sasha's sample against our staging data: 

- Reproduction: confirmed reduced extraction accuracy on the billing intents when running the prompt_set_v3.json and their sample set. Baseline (v5.1) precision on that subset was 96.3%; post-update (v5.2 auto-rollout) it's 89.7%.
- Root cause (initial): tokenization/decoder tweak in 5.2 that improves general throughput but alters boundary handling for short, templated billing messages. The change is visible in model_diff_5.2_vs_5.1.txt (attached).

Mitigation options:
A) Pin their high-priority routing to redwood/opt-7b-q4f-v5.1 (recommended immediate fix). Pinning is a config change (no model redeploy) and we can enact within ~15 minutes once approved.
B) Canary + dynamic routing: send a sample percentage (5-10%) to v5.2 for live monitoring while keeping majority traffic on v5.1 — takes ~30 minutes to configure and 24-48h to collect stable metrics.
C) Full rollback of the auto-rollout to v5.1 globally — takes ~2-4 hours and requires product/infra sign-off; higher blast radius.

Notes on side-effects: pinning is low-risk and reversible. If we apply pin at the routing layer for their account/route, their SLA and throughput targets will be unaffected. We should also schedule a deeper diff analysis and a short backfill run (48h) to validate fixes once engineers propose a 5.2 patch (likely tokenization fix).

I've attached the diff and a short command doc for pin/rollback: https://docs.redwood.com/runbook/rollback-guidance

Requesting approval to apply option A for Acme now. Marissa — if you can confirm with Sasha/Tom, I’ll execute and monitor.

—Rishi
